profile.summary: GenSLM (genome-scale language model) is a family of autoregressive language models that read DNA coding sequence as codons, three nucleotides per token. The foundation models were pretrained on over 110 million prokaryotic gene sequences, and a SARS-CoV-2 model was fine-tuned on 1.5 million viral genomes to track the virus's evolution and pick out variants of concern. The released code computes sequence embeddings and generates new sequences.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper: Abstract; Introduction, contributions; Figure 1 caption. README: Usage

summary_quotes.text: By pretraining on over 110 million prokaryotic gene sequences and finetuning a SARS-CoV-2-specific model on 1.5 million genomes, we show that GenSLMs can accurately and rapidly identify variants of concern.
The inputs to GenSLM are nucleotide sequences, encoded at the codon level (every three nucleotide represents a codon; hence the 20 natural amino acid language is described by 64 codons).
Use GenSLMs to compute sequence embeddings for downsteam tasks, generate synthetic sequences, or easily extend them to your own application.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: GenSLMs are generative pre-trained transformers (GPT-style causal language models) with a codon-level tokeniser. The released foundation models load GPT-NeoX architecture files (the 25M file declares GPTNeoXForCausalLM with 8 layers, hidden size 512 and 8 attention heads) and a 69-token codon vocabulary, and were trained at four sizes from 25 million to 25 billion parameters with a maximum sequence length of 2,048 tokens on individual genes from BV-BRC. The 25M and 250M models were then fine-tuned on SARS-CoV-2 genomes with sequence length 10,240 tokens; the larger sizes ran out of GPU memory at that length. The paper also describes a hierarchical model in which a diffusion model guides a codon-level transformer to cover whole genomes; the README points to a separate repository for it.

We, therefore, trained GenSLM foundation models on a wide set of parameter scales ranging from 25 million to 25 billion, with a maximum sequence length of 2,048 tokens on the BV-BRC dataset
we fine-tuned the foundation model GenSLMs using a maximum sequence length of 10,240 tokens for the 25M and 250M model sizes on the SARS-CoV-2 datasets
training on the 10,240 length SARS-CoV-2 data was infeasible on GPU clusters due to out-of-memory errors during attention computation
Please refer to this codebase for diffusion model usage: https://github.com/da03/hierarchical_diffusion_LM

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The inference code names five model IDs: genslm_25M_patric, genslm_250M_patric, genslm_2.5B_patric and genslm_25B_patric (foundation models, 2,048 tokens) and genslm_25M_covid (SARS-CoV-2 model, 10,240 tokens). Each ID maps to a fixed weight file name, for example patric_25m_epoch01-val_loss_0.57_bias_removed.pt. Weights are downloaded from a Globus endpoint; the README warns that files fetched before 3 May 2023 have a name space issue and should be downloaded again. The COVID model's weights are available on enquiry. A result should name the model ID, the weight file name and the repository commit (this page read 6622c47e).

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Autoregressive (causal) nucleotide language model with codon tokenisation; foundation models plus a SARS-CoV-2 fine-tuned model.

quotes.text: LLMs with codon tokenization (with 2.5 and 25 billion trainable parameters) to date

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: GPT-style transformer. The released checkpoints load GPT-NeoX causal language model configurations (GPTNeoXForCausalLM) through Hugging Face transformers; the 25M configuration has 8 layers, hidden size 512, 8 attention heads and rotary position embeddings.

quotes.text: Generative Pre-trained Transformers (GPT) (on individual gene sequences)

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: Nucleotide gene sequences as strings, tokenised into codons (three nucleotides per token).

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Next-token (codon) probabilities, hidden-state embeddings (the README averages the last layer over the sequence, giving 512 values per sequence for the 25M model) and generated sequences.

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: 25M, 250M, 2.5B and 25B foundation models. The architecture files are named neox_25,290,752, neox_244,464,576, neox_2,533,931,008 and neox_25,076,188,032. The COVID model uses the 25M architecture with 10,240 position embeddings.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: Foundation models: more than 110 million unique prokaryotic gene sequences from BV-BRC. SARS-CoV-2 fine-tuning: more than 1.5 million high-quality BV-BRC complete genomes, after removing genomes under 29,000 bp or with more than 1% ambiguous bases. A GenSLM-25M model shown in the paper was trained only on the first year of SARS-CoV-2 data, about 85,000 genomes.

facts.label: Known versions
facts.value: genslm_25M_patric, genslm_250M_patric, genslm_2.5B_patric, genslm_25B_patric and genslm_25M_covid. The hierarchical diffusion model lives in a separate repository.

facts.label: Training cutoff
facts.value: Not reported. The paper does not give the BV-BRC download date; one 25M model was trained on the first year of SARS-CoV-2 data only.

facts.label: Context limits
facts.value: 2,048 codon tokens for the foundation models; 10,240 tokens for the SARS-CoV-2 model.

run_guide.summary: Install the genslm package, place the 25M foundation model weights in the working directory and compute averaged embeddings for two example gene sequences.
prerequisites: Python with pip. The README example uses a GPU when present, else CPU. The sources do not state memory needs.
The weight file patric_25m_epoch01-val_loss_0.57_bias_removed.pt from the Globus endpoint.
Code is MIT. No licence is stated for the weights.

steps.title: Compute embeddings
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
import torch
import numpy as np
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader
from genslm import GenSLM, SequenceDataset

model = GenSLM("genslm_25M_patric")
model.eval()
device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
model.to(device)

sequences = [
    "ATGAAAGTAACCGTTGTTGGAGCAGGTGCAGTTGGTGCAAGTTGCGCAGAATATATTGCA",
    "ATTAAAGATTTCGCATCTGAAGTTGTTTTGTTAGACATTAAAGAAGGTTATGCCGAAGGT",
]
dataset = SequenceDataset(sequences, model.seq_length, model.tokenizer)
dataloader = DataLoader(dataset)

embeddings = []
with torch.no_grad():
    for batch in dataloader:
        outputs = model(
            batch["input_ids"].to(device),
            batch["attention_mask"].to(device),
            output_hidden_states=True,
        )
        emb = outputs.hidden_states[-1].detach().cpu().numpy()
        emb = np.mean(emb, axis=1)
        embeddings.append(emb)

embeddings = np.concatenate(embeddings)
print(embeddings.shape)
PY
steps.explanation: The README embedding example wrapped in a shell heredoc. The model_cache_dir argument (a Colab Google Drive path in the README) is dropped so the default, the current directory, is used; comments are removed and the final bare expression is wrapped in print().

outputs: An array of averaged last-layer embeddings; the README shows shape (2, 512) for the two example sequences.

notes: Parameter counts are taken from the architecture file names in inference.py (for example neox_25,290,752.json), which appear to encode the parameter count; the paper's Table 1 with the stated counts was not in the fetched page text. The COVID model's count is left null because its architecture file adds 10,240 position embeddings to the 25M design. The record sits under RNA (RNAGym leaderboard), but GenSLM is a DNA codon model trained on prokaryotic genes and SARS-CoV-2 genomes. The paper is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, so its page is hashed and not stored.
